title: project export lowercases APEXlang file and folder names
workaround: Run `apex export -applicationid <id> -exptype APEXLANG -dir src/database/<schema>/apex_apps/f<id> -f` after `project export`.
prompt: Remove the exported application folder, run `project export -o APEX.<app_id>` in the test repo, and compare every mixed-case file or folder name of the baseline export with the exported names.
successCriteria: Every mixed-case name in the baseline export (for example static-files/img/mixedCaseImageName.webp) is exported with the same case.

title: project export corrupts binary APEX static files
workaround: Run `apex export -applicationid <id> -exptype APEXLANG -dir src/database/<schema>/apex_apps/f<id> -f` after `project export`; it rewrites the binary files correctly.
prompt: Remove the exported application folder, run `project export -o APEX.<app_id>` in the test repo, and compare each binary file of the baseline export (static-files icons and images) byte for byte with the exported file.
successCriteria: Every binary file is byte-identical to the baseline (same SHA-1).

apexlang.oracleStatus: not reported (the readable-mode fix of 26.2.2 does not cover APEXlang mode)

title: project export keeps files of APEX components deleted in APEX
workaround: Delete src/database/<schema>/apex_apps/f<id> before `project export`, or run `apex export -applicationid <id> -exptype APEXLANG -dir src/database/<schema>/apex_apps/f<id> -f` after it.
prompt: On an isolated branch: export the application into an empty apex_apps folder (this version's layout) and commit it, remove page APEX_SPARE_PAGE from the installed application (apex import of a copy without it), run `project export -o APEX.<app_id>` again over the committed folder, and check the page file is gone. The commit is needed because in APEXlang mode project export refuses to overwrite uncommitted changes (021). Only when the file is left behind, and in readable mode, the workaround `apex export -f` is checked and reported in the Workaround column. Re-import the baseline application afterwards.
successCriteria: After project export, the export folder contains no file for page 100 (p00100-*.apx).

title: project export -o does not export synonyms
workaround: Export the synonym together with its table (`project export -o <table>`) or run a full `project export`.
prompt: Create table REG_004_T and synonym REG_004_SYN for it in the project schema, run `project export -o REG_004_SYN`, and look for synonyms/reg_004_syn.sql. If it is missing, run `project export -o REG_004_T` as a control: the synonym is exported along with its table, which proves it is exportable. Drop both objects and restore src afterwards.
successCriteria: `project export -o REG_004_SYN` writes src/database/<schema>/synonyms/reg_004_syn.sql.

title: APEXlang source written by project export fails apex validate
oracleStatus: not reported separately (consequence of the lowercasing bug, 001)
workaround: Run `apex export -applicationid <id> -exptype APEXLANG -dir src/database/<schema>/apex_apps/f<id> -f` after `project export`.
prompt: Export the application with `project export -o APEX.<app_id>` into an empty apex_apps folder and run `apex validate -input <folder with application.apx>`. The lowercased static file name no longer matches the reference in static-files.apx, so APEXlang compilation reports REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND.
successCriteria: `apex validate` on the exported APEXlang folder prints `Validation successful`.

title: project export does not use the documented f<app_id>/<app-alias>/ folder
workaround: None; stay on SQLcl 26.1.
prompt: Export the application into an empty apex_apps folder and find application.apx. The documented location is f<app_id>/<app-alias>/ (alias in lower case), beside f<app_id>.sql. Readable mode: SQLcl 26.1 writes it there; 26.2.2 flattens it into f<app_id>/. APEXlang mode: 26.2.2 writes it to apex_apps/<app-alias>/.
successCriteria: application.apx is in src/database/<schema>/apex_apps/f<app_id>/<app-alias>/.

apexlang.oracleStatus: intended by Oracle (Neil Fernandez-Oracle, Sep 2026), but contradicts the documentation

title: project export -o APEX.<id> exports users and data that were not requested
workaround: Add `export_type != 'TABLES_DML'` and `export_type != 'ALL_USERS'` to .dbtools/filters/project.filters (the test project keeps them between --TEST-007 BEGIN and --TEST-007 END).
prompt: The baseline filters hold the workaround between `--TEST-007 BEGIN` and `--TEST-007 END`. Restore src, export with `project export -o APEX.<app_id>` and list src files changed outside the application folder: with the workaround there should be none. Then remove the block, restore src, export again and list them again: that second list decides the result. Seen with any -o export in SQLcl 26.2.2 (e.g. -o <package> also exported 14 users), not only APEX applications.
successCriteria: Without the TEST-007 filters, nothing outside src/database/<schema>/apex_apps/ changes.

title: project stage refuses the APEX controller generated by an earlier SQLcl version
workaround: Delete dist/releases/apex/f<id>/f<id>.xml before `project stage`.
prompt: On a branch from the baseline (staged by SQLcl 26.1), delete a page in APEX, export the application, commit, and run `project stage`. Stage must regenerate dist/releases/apex/f<app_id>/f<app_id>.xml instead of stopping with "has been edited and stage will not overwrite it automatically".
successCriteria: `project stage` prints `Stage processing completed`.

title: Switching to APEXlang mode leaves the legacy SQL controller in apex.changelog.xml
workaround: Remove the legacy dist/releases/apex/f<id> folder and its <include> from apex.changelog.xml by hand.
prompt: In APEXlang mode (the runner has set apex.apexlang=true on top of the baseline), export the application into an empty apex_apps folder, commit, run `project stage`, and read the <include> entries of dist/releases/apex/apex.changelog.xml.
successCriteria: apex.changelog.xml no longer includes f<app_id>/f<app_id>.xml once the APEXlang controller is added.

title: project export exports ORDS of the connected user instead of the project schemas
workaround: Export ORDS while connected as the schema itself (SCHEMA_CONN). The undocumented setting export.ords.ordsAdmin=true does not help: no code reads it in 26.1 or 26.2.
prompt: The baseline REST-enables the project schema with module regression.dept. Restore src, remove src/database/<schema>/ords, run `project export -debug` with the deployer connection, and look for the module in the re-exported ords folder. The debug log shows `ORA-20012: Schema not REST enabled : <deployer>` from ords_export.export_schema() called without a schema.
successCriteria: src/database/<schema>/ords/ is exported again and contains the module regression.dept.

title: project stage regenerates ORDS changesets even when ORDS did not change
oracleStatus: bug 38688471 reopened (danmcghan-Oracle, Jan 29 2026); not reproducible in the test project with SQLcl 26.1.2, so treated as fixed
workaround: Discard the regenerated ORDS files before committing.
prompt: On a branch, connected as the schema (SCHEMA_CONN): create table REG_012_T, run a full `project export` (ORDS is re-exported unchanged), restore the application folder, commit, run `project stage`, and list dist files with ORDS in their path. Drop the table afterwards.
successCriteria: project stage writes no ORDS files when ORDS did not change.

title: project export appends a semicolon to a view's trailing line comment
workaround: Edit the exported view file and remove the semicolon from the comment line.
prompt: Create view REG_013_V whose query ends with a line comment (`from dept -- reg_013 trailing line comment`), run `project export -o REG_013_V`, and read the comment line in the exported file. SQLcl 25.3.2 wrote `-- reg_013 trailing line comment;` followed by a separate `;`. Drop the view afterwards.
successCriteria: The exported comment line does not end with a semicolon; the statement terminator is on its own line.

title: APEXlang mode (apex.apexlang=true) does not use the documented f<app_id>/<app-alias>/ folder
oracleStatus: intended by Oracle (Neil Fernandez-Oracle, Sep 2026), but contradicts the documentation
workaround: None; do not enable apex.apexlang.
prompt: Merged into 006, which now runs in both modes (006 in APEXlang mode is this test). Kept so the number is not reused. Run `project config set -name apex.apexlang -value true` (SQLcl 26.1 has no such setting; the export must then simply be unchanged), export the application into an empty apex_apps folder and find application.apx. Restore project.config.json afterwards.
successCriteria: application.apx is in src/database/<schema>/apex_apps/f<app_id>/<app-alias>/.

title: project stage fails with hash errors on APEX supporting object scripts
workaround: None in 26.1; upgrade to 26.2.
prompt: On a branch, add a supporting object with an upgrade script (fixture/ in the test folder) to the application through apex import, export the application, commit, and run `project stage`. SQLcl 26.1 stops with "The hash value of the file supportingobjectscript.sql is incorrect and can not be automatically adjusted (hard object)" and "Unrecoverable hash issues present". The test removes dist/releases/apex/f<id>/f<id>.xml first so that issue 008 does not interfere.
successCriteria: project stage prints `Stage processing completed`.

title: stage.change.changeStyle=multiple puts each staged statement in its own changeset
oracleStatus: setting confirmed on the forum; to be exposed through project config as the fix of the logged bug
workaround: Add "change": {"changeStyle": "multiple"} to the stage object in .dbtools/project.config.json.
prompt: The baseline .dbtools/project.config.json sets stage.change.changeStyle to multiple (an Oracle-suggested setting that `project config set` does not expose yet; forum 8780). On a branch, add two columns and a check constraint to DEPT, export DEPT, commit, run `project stage`, and compare the number of `-- changeset` lines with the number of statements in the staged dept.sql. With the default (single) all statements share one changeset, in 26.1 and 26.2. Drop the columns afterwards.
successCriteria: Every statement in the staged dept.sql has its own changeset.

title: Deployed APEX changesets are recorded with different filename separators in DATABASECHANGELOG and DATABASECHANGELOG_ACTIONS on Windows, so they redeploy every time
workaround: Windows-only teams: update DATABASECHANGELOG.filename to the backslash form, e.g. update databasechangelog set filename = 'releases\apex\f100\f100.xml' where id = 'INSTALL_100'. No workaround for mixed Windows/macOS/Linux teams.
prompt: Nothing extra is deployed: the reset at the start of the run installs the baseline from dist (dist/install.sql, lb update) with the SQLcl under test. Connected as the installer, compare id, author and filename of the APEX changesets (id INSTALL%) in DATABASECHANGELOG and DATABASECHANGELOG_ACTIONS: select filename, id, author from databasechangelog where id like 'INSTALL%'; select filename, id, author, status from databasechangelog_actions where id like 'INSTALL%'. Then, from dist, run the lb update command of dist/install.sql with update replaced by status (same -def properties, so ${...} substitutions give the same checksums; e.g. `lb status -changelog-file releases/main.changelog.xml -def env/test.properties`) and look for INSTALL_ changesets listed as not deployed. On Windows with the bug, the changelog has releases/apex/f<id>/f<id>.xml and the actions releases\apex\f<id>\f<id>.xml, so Liquibase, matching on (id, author, filename), never sees the changeset as run. Only meaningful on Windows.
successCriteria: Every INSTALL% row of DATABASECHANGELOG has a DATABASECHANGELOG_ACTIONS row with the same id, author and filename, and lb status lists neither f<app_id>.xml nor INSTALL_<app_id>.

title: Staged ORDS changeset installs into the deploying user instead of the project schema
workaround: Install ORDS through ORDS_ADMIN with p_schema in a custom changeset (as the test project does), or deploy the ORDS changeset connected as the schema.
prompt: Inactive: the suite does not deploy. ORDS is covered by 011 (export as the installer), 012 and 019 (export and stage as the schema). The baseline keeps the schema-connection ORDS export in dist/releases/ords/ but does not install it (commented out in main.changelog.xml). As the installer, drop the ORDS definitions of the schema and the installer and run `lb update -changelog-file releases/ords/ords.changelog.xml` from dist. The changeset (author <SCHEMA>) calls ORDS.ENABLE_SCHEMA / DEFINE_MODULE, which act on the session current schema; check which schema owns module regression.dept. Afterwards restore the baseline ORDS through the ORDS_ADMIN custom changeset.
successCriteria: After lb update as the deployer, the module belongs to the project schema.

title: Connected as the schema, project export exports ORDS and project stage leaves unchanged ORDS alone
oracleStatus: works (the baseline ORDS was exported and staged this way with SQLcl 26.1.2)
workaround: Not needed when connected as the schema; as the installer ORDS is not exported at all (011).
prompt: On a branch, connected as the schema (SCHEMA_CONN), without changing ORDS: remove src/database/<schema>/ords, run a full `project export`, and compare the ords folder with the baseline. Restore the application folder, commit whatever else changed, run `project stage`, and list dist files with ORDS in their path. Nothing is deployed.
successCriteria: The ords folder is exported and identical to the baseline, and project stage writes no ORDS files.

title: project stage fails with "Unable to save changelog, changelog is empty" for a change of more than one statement
workaround: None found: changeStyle single, multiple or not set all fail the same way.
prompt: On a branch, add a column and a check constraint to EMP, `project export -o EMP`, commit. Then from that commit run `project stage` three times: with stage.change.changeStyle removed from project.config.json, set to single, and set to multiple. Each time check that stage completes and stage.changelog.xml includes emp.sql. SQLcl 26.3 writes emp.sql but leaves stage.changelog.xml empty and stops with the error. The comment reports, per setting, how many statements and changesets emp.sql has, which shows whether the setting still has any effect.
successCriteria: project stage completes and stage.changelog.xml includes the EMP changeset with every changeStyle setting.

title: A second project export of an APEX application, with nothing changed, fails in APEXlang mode
workaround: Commit the application folder after each export, before exporting again.
prompt: Export the application into an empty apex_apps folder, delete application.apx from the exported folder, then run `project export -o APEX.<app_id>` again straight away, without committing and without any change in APEX, and check application.apx is back. (Comparing the two exports is not enough: in APEXlang mode the second export writes nothing, reports "Exported 0 objects" and "APEXlang export target has tracked or untracked Git changes", and the folder simply keeps the first export.)
successCriteria: The second export exports the application again: application.apx, deleted before it, is recreated.

title: After the application deployment is regenerated from scratch, project stage writes more than the controller of the APEX mode (APEXlang: legacy f<app_id> entries come back)
workaround: APEXlang mode: comment out the legacy f<app_id> entries in apex.changelog.xml after every stage.
prompt: On a branch, in the APEX mode under test: remove src/database/<schema>/apex_apps/f<app_id>, dist/releases/apex/f<app_id> and the f<app_id> include of dist/releases/apex/apex.changelog.xml, commit; `project export -o APEX.<app_id>`, commit; `project stage`. Read the includes of apex.changelog.xml and list dist/releases/apex/f<app_id>. Readable mode (the control case): stage puts f<app_id>/f<app_id>.xml back and a regenerated f<app_id>.sql where the old one was. APEXlang mode: stage should add only <alias>/<alias>.xml, but also writes f<app_id> entries and files.
successCriteria: apex.changelog.xml has exactly one include, f<app_id>/f<app_id>.xml (readable, with f<app_id>.sql regenerated) or <alias>/<alias>.xml (APEXlang, with no f<app_id> files generated).

title: APEX deployment with the schema in two workspaces: APEXlang fails ("Multiple workspaces available") and records the failed changeset as run; readable must deploy once
workaround: None known for the generated APEXlang install.
prompt: Needs the baseline schema mapped to two or more APEX workspaces. Regenerate the deployment as in 022, comment out every apex.changelog.xml include except the controller of the mode, commit, deploy with dist/install.sql as the installer, then deploy again. Readable mode (the control case): the first deploy runs INSTALL_<app_id> without errors, the second skips it. APEXlang mode: the generated install does not pass the workspace, so it stops with "Multiple workspaces available, use the workspaceId or the workspace option", and Liquibase still records the INSTALL changeset in DATABASECHANGELOG. The database is reset before and after the test.
successCriteria: The first deploy runs the APEX changeset of the controller without errors (with an error, the changeset must not be recorded as run), and a second deploy with nothing changed does not run it again.
